claims.text: The onset of phase transition in initially solid FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles is governed by the interplay between configurational entropy and thermal expansion.
The progression of phase transition in initially solid FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles is governed by the interplay between configurational entropy and thermal expansion.
Combining in situ characterization with molecular-dynamics simulations can elucidate the phase-transition behavior of FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles.
Molecular dynamics has been used to model temperature-dependent properties of FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy alloys.
Thermal expansion is a relevant structural mediator for the phase transition of FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles.
Configurational entropy is a relevant structural mediator for the phase transition of FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles.
The FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticle phase transition will occur over a temperature range 100–200 K higher than the melting point of pure Fe.
Nanoparticle size and shape define relevant boundary conditions for the proposed phase-transition behavior.
The exact transition temperature range and behavior may depend on FeNiCrCoCu composition.
The exact transition temperature range and behavior may depend on processing conditions.
